observations.text: SP, due to a delayed and shallow bank input at the leader's pitch out signal, did not roll into the pre-determined bank at the pre-determined airspeed and did not establish the briefed spacing, with the result that airspeed diverged by 26 knots from the pre-determined value and the exit heading settled 15 degrees off the leader's, both beyond the allowed tolerances. The IP directed the bank correction and applied part of the power inputs to re-establish the spacing. Further practice in pitch out timing and bank control is required.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not use the pre-determined bank to build the briefed spacing after the leader's command and did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid way, with the result of an altitude excursion of 380 feet during the turn, beyond the allowed tolerance. The IP directed the recovery to the briefed altitude and executed part of the repositioning to set the spacing.

SP, due to an unstabilized bank that was allowed to increase through the pitch out, did not hold the pre-determined airspeed and did not roll out on the briefed exit heading, with the result of an airspeed deviation reaching 20 knots and an exit heading deviation of 10 degrees, at the limit of the allowed tolerances. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompts, and no intervention on the controls was required.

SP, due to an absent cross-check of aircraft state against the primary flight instruments while attention remained outside on the leader, did not maintain the briefed altitude and the pre-determined airspeed through the pitch out, with the result of an altitude deviation of 300 feet and an airspeed deviation of 20 knots, at the limit of the allowed tolerances. Both deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal prompts. No intervention on the controls was required.

SP, due to a late power reduction at the entry of the pitch out, did not hold the pre-determined airspeed throughout the turn, with the result of an airspeed deviation of 15 knots and an exit heading 8 degrees off the briefed value. Both errors were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention, and the briefed spacing was established.

SP, due to distraction from the primary scan by an unrelated switch action during the pitch out, did not keep the A/C at the briefed altitude while building the spacing, with the result of an altitude deviation of 230 feet. The deviation was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, with the exit heading contained within 5 degrees of the briefed value.

SP executed the pitch out on the leader's command and established the briefed spacing within the desired standards. However, the pre-determined bank was set with a small delay on two occasions, leaving airspeed deviations up to 10 knots and altitude deviations up to 140 feet, at the edge of the allowed tolerance, while control of the A/C remained smooth and solid and the exit heading was held within 5 degrees. Marginal performance for the Training Section - promptness in setting the pre-determined bank at the leader's signal is expected to improve.

SP executed the pitch out immediately on the leader's command, according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual, setting the pre-determined bank and airspeed without hesitation. Spacing was built exactly as briefed and control of the A/C was exceptionally smooth and solid, with altitude, airspeed and exit heading deviations negligible throughout the maneuver. Visual contact with the leader was maintained at all times and no blind situation developed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an abrupt and oversized bank input at the pitch out, did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid way and did not establish the briefed spacing on the leader, with the result of an altitude loss of 420 feet inside the turn, beyond the allowed tolerance. The IP directed the recovery and applied part of the control inputs to re-establish the briefed altitude and the spacing. Further practice in bank and pitch coordination during the pitch out is required.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the A/C's position relative to the leader after the pitch out, did not handle the resulting blind situation correctly and in a timely manner and did not build the briefed spacing, with the result that airspeed diverged 28 knots from the pre-determined value before visual contact was regained. The IP directed the blind procedure and executed part of the repositioning.

SP, due to insufficient anticipation of the roll-out at the end of the pitch out, did not stop the turn on the briefed exit heading and did not hold the pre-determined airspeed, with the result of an exit heading deviation of 10 degrees and an airspeed deviation of 19 knots, at the limit of the allowed tolerances. The errors were recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompts, without intervention on the controls.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with the radio call, the lookout on the leader and A/C control attempted simultaneously, did not maintain the briefed altitude while establishing the spacing, with the result of an altitude deviation of 300 feet, at the limit of the allowed tolerance. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal prompt, and no intervention on the controls was required.

SP executed the pitch out on the leader's command and established the spacing within the desired standards for this training unit. However, the pre-determined bank was allowed to vary during the turn, leaving airspeed deviations up to 14 knots and an exit heading 8 degrees off the briefed value, each one recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - steadiness of the pre-determined bank through the pitch out is expected to improve.

SP executed the pitch out promptly on the leader's command, setting the pre-determined bank and airspeed according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual. Spacing was established as briefed and control of the A/C was smooth and solid, with altitude held within 150 feet, airspeed within 10 knots and the exit heading within 5 degrees. No verbal prompting from the IP was required at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the pitch out and the spacing build-up to the standards of the Techniques and Procedures Manual, with the pre-determined bank and airspeed set on the leader's command without any prompting. Control of the A/C was exceptionally smooth and solid and the deviations in altitude, airspeed and exit heading were negligible throughout the maneuver. Visual contact with the leader was never lost and the spacing was left ready for the subsequent rejoin without correction. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect bank and power technique at the entry of the pitch out, could not establish the briefed spacing without assistance, with the result of an airspeed excursion of 30 knots from the pre-determined value and an exit heading 18 degrees off the briefed one, both beyond the allowed tolerances. The IP directed the maneuver and executed part of the bank and power corrections. Further study of the pitch out procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP, due to an incomplete mental model of the pitch out sequence that was not updated when the leader's command came earlier than briefed, did not initiate the turn at the pre-determined airspeed and bank and did not build the briefed spacing, with the result of an altitude excursion of 450 feet, beyond the allowed tolerance. The IP directed the sequence and executed part of the recovery to the briefed altitude.

SP executed the pitch out at the level expected for this training unit, initiating the turn after the IP's verbal reminder of the leader's command and setting the pre-determined bank once it was called from the front cockpit. Spacing was built with airspeed deviations reaching 20 knots and an exit heading 10 degrees off the briefed value, recognized and corrected with delay but without intervention on the controls. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent recognition of the pitch out signal and prompt setting of the pre-determined bank are expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP recognized the leader's pitch out command without prompting and set the pre-determined bank and airspeed unaided. Minor errors in power management left airspeed deviating up to 15 knots and the exit heading 7 degrees off the briefed value, each one recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Spacing was established close to the briefed value and control of the A/C was smooth. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the pitch out immediately on the leader's command, according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual, holding the pre-determined bank and airspeed throughout the turn. Spacing was established exactly as briefed, with altitude held within 150 feet, airspeed within 10 knots and the exit heading within 5 degrees, and control of the A/C was smooth and solid. No verbal prompting was required at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the pitch out and established the spacing to the standards of the Techniques and Procedures Manual, anticipating the leader's command and setting the pre-determined bank and airspeed without any prompting. Deviations in altitude, airspeed and exit heading were negligible throughout the maneuver and control of the A/C was exceptionally smooth and solid. Visual contact with the leader was maintained continuously, leaving the formation set up for the following maneuver without correction. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the pitch out at the level expected for this training unit, with the IP directing the recognition of the leader's command and calling the bank and the power to be set. Spacing was built only while the IP prompted each correction, and part of the roll-out on the briefed exit heading was executed from the front cockpit. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent execution of the pitch out and of the spacing corrections is expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP, after the pre-flight study of the pitch out procedure, initiated the turn on the leader's command, with a verbal reminder from the IP required for the pre-determined bank. Airspeed was allowed to build 20 knots above the pre-determined value and the exit heading settled 10 degrees off the briefed one, at the limit of the allowed tolerances, both corrected with delay after the IP's prompts. No part of the maneuver had to be executed by the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP recognized the leader's pitch out command without prompting and set the pre-determined bank unaided. Minor errors in power management left airspeed deviating up to 14 knots and altitude up to 220 feet, each one recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Spacing was established close to the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the pitch out promptly on the leader's command, according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual, holding the pre-determined bank and airspeed through the turn. Spacing was established as briefed and control of the A/C was smooth and solid, with altitude held within 150 feet, airspeed within 10 knots and the exit heading within 5 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the pitch out and the spacing build-up to the standards of the Techniques and Procedures Manual, anticipating the leader's command and setting the pre-determined bank and airspeed without any prompting. Deviations in altitude, airspeed and exit heading were negligible throughout the maneuver and control of the A/C was exceptionally smooth and solid. Visual contact with the leader was never lost and no blind situation developed. Above end of block MIF achieved.
